```{r setup, include=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This reference displays code without running it. Examples are independent recipes,
not one script to execute from top to bottom. Argument templates include required
placeholders; replace them with your objects. See the Orbi vignette for a complete
analysis.

## Processing logic

Each filtering function takes a prepared dataset and returns an updated
object containing the retained features, removed feature IDs, and
filter-specific results.

- **Individual filtering calls follow your chosen order.** Pass the result
  of one step to the next. Each step operates on the features retained by
  the preceding steps, so changing the order can change the results.
- **Each filtering stage can be applied once per object:** blank, MS, QC
  and peak filtering. To change settings or repeat a stage, start again
  from the saved object immediately before that stage.
- **`mc_run()` uses a fixed stage order:** blank → MS → QC → peak.
  Stages set to `NULL` are skipped.
- **MS subfilters run sequentially in a fixed order:** isotopes → adducts
  → neutral losses → in-source fragments → mispicked ions →
  ringing/saturated ions. Only selected subfilters run. Their order in
  the `filters` vector does not change the processing order.
- **QC and peak criteria are combined within their respective stages.**
  A feature must satisfy every selected criterion. For QC, `mode`
  determines how results from the evaluated groups are combined.
- **Plotting uses the stored filtering results.** It does not rerun
  filtering. A stage-specific plot requires that stage to have been applied.
- **Final tables and exports use the current retained features.**
  `mc_final_table()`, `mc_write_table()` and `mc_export()` default to
  `format = "input"`, restoring the original input-table layout.


## Prepare bundled data

```{r prepare-example}
library(MetaboCensoR)
peak_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "orbi_iimn_gnps_quant.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported <- mc_prepare(
  peak_file, type = "mzmine",
  sample_keywords = c(".mzML", "Peak area")
)
metadata_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_metadata(
  metadata_file, sample_names = imported$sample_cols,
  sample_col = "Sample name", label_col = "Label"
)
```

## Download optional spectra and adducts

```{r downloads}
base_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plyush1993/",
  "MetaboCensoR_Examples/main/orbi/"
)
mgf_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".mgf")
adduct_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
download.file(paste0(base_url, "orbi_iimn_gnps.mgf"),
              mgf_file, mode = "wb")
download.file(paste0(base_url, "adducts%20%28nontarget%20%2B%202xH2O%29.csv"),
              adduct_file, mode = "wb")
spectra <- mc_read_mgf(mgf_file)
```

## Complete MS and peak parameter dictionaries

These are defaults. Only the tolerance matching
`"da"` or `"ppm"` is used. Explicit `filters` in a filtering call override the
enable flags. Use `"positive"` or `"negative"` for polarity.

```{r ms-defaults}
ms_options <- mc_ms_parameters(
  # ISOTOPE FILTERING
  # Enable isotope filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit
  # filters vector overrides this flag; use "isotopes" to select isotope
  # filtering explicitly.
  enable_iso2 = TRUE,
  # Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of a
  # candidate isotope and its parent feature. Values range from 0 to 1; higher
  # cutoffs require more similar profiles.
  iso_cor2 = 0.8,
  # Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between a candidate isotope
  # and its parent feature.
  iso_rt2 = 0.01,
  # Mass-tolerance unit for isotope matching: "da" uses iso_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses
  # iso_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used.
  iso_tol_type2 = "da",
  # Absolute mass tolerance in Da for isotope matching. Used only when
  # iso_tol_type2 = "da".
  iso_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  # Relative mass tolerance in ppm for isotope matching. Used only when
  # iso_tol_type2 = "ppm".
  iso_ppm2 = 10,
  # Maximum charge state searched for isotope relationships. For example, 3
  # searches charge states 1, 2 and 3.
  iso_zmax2 = 3,
  # Maximum isotope order k searched. Expected isotope spacing is 1.00336 * k / z
  # Da, for orders 1 through iso_n2 and charges 1 through iso_zmax2.
  iso_n2 = 1,
  # Number of additional dimer-pattern isotope shifts searched: 1.00336 * (j +
  # 0.5) Da for j from 1 through iso_nd2.
  iso_nd2 = 3,
  # ADDUCT FILTERING
  # Enable adduct filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit
  # filters vector overrides this flag; use "adducts" to select adduct filtering
  # explicitly.
  enable_add2 = TRUE,
  # Ionization polarity used to select adduct definitions: "positive" or
  # "negative". Set nl_pol2 separately if neutral-loss filtering is also used.
  add_pol2 = "positive",
  # Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of features
  # proposed to belong to the same adduct family. Values range from 0 to 1;
  # higher cutoffs require more similar profiles.
  add_cor2 = 0.8,
  # Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between features proposed to
  # belong to the same adduct family.
  add_rt2 = 0.005,
  # Mass-tolerance unit for adduct matching: "da" uses add_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses
  # add_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used.
  add_tol_type2 = "da",
  # Absolute mass tolerance in Da for adduct matching. Used only when
  # add_tol_type2 = "da".
  add_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  # Relative mass tolerance in ppm for adduct matching. Used only when
  # add_tol_type2 = "ppm".
  add_ppm2 = 10,
  # Minimum candidate neutral mass in Da for adduct annotation. Candidate neutral
  # masses must be strictly greater than this threshold.
  add_min_nm2 = 50,
  # If TRUE, restrict the total retention-time spread of an adduct family to
  # add_rt2 minutes, in addition to pairwise matching.
  add_strict_rt2 = TRUE,
  # Prefer selected ion forms when choosing adduct-family representatives.
  # Retain the most intense qualifying preferred feature, or the most intense feature overall
  # if none qualify.
  add_prefer2 = FALSE,
  # Character vector of preferred ion names, matching the adduct definitions.
  # For example, c("M+H", "M+Na").
  add_preferred2 = NULL,
  # Maximum intensity decrease (%) from the family's highest mean intensity 
  # for a preferred representative.
  add_prefer_pct2 = 10,
  # NEUTRAL-LOSS FILTERING
  # Enable neutral-loss filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit
  # filters vector overrides this flag; use "neutral_losses" to select neutral-
  # loss filtering explicitly.
  enable_nl2 = FALSE,
  # Ionization polarity used to select neutral-loss definitions: "positive" or
  # "negative". Set add_pol2 separately if adduct filtering is also used.
  nl_pol2 = "positive",
  # Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of features
  # proposed to differ by a listed neutral loss. Values range from 0 to 1; higher
  # cutoffs require more similar profiles.
  nl_cor2 = 0.95,
  # Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between features proposed to
  # differ by a listed neutral loss.
  nl_rt2 = 0.002,
  # Mass-tolerance unit for neutral-loss matching: "da" uses nl_mz_tol2; "ppm"
  # uses nl_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used.
  nl_tol_type2 = "da",
  # Absolute mass tolerance in Da for neutral-loss matching. Used only when
  # nl_tol_type2 = "da".
  nl_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  # Relative mass tolerance in ppm for neutral-loss matching. Used only when
  # nl_tol_type2 = "ppm".
  nl_ppm2 = 10,
  # IN-SOURCE FRAGMENT FILTERING
  # Enable in-source fragment filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An
  # explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "isf" to select in-source
  # fragment filtering explicitly.
  enable_isf2 = FALSE,
  # Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of a
  # candidate in-source fragment and its precursor feature. Values range from 0
  # to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles.
  isf_cor2 = 0.95,
  # Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between a candidate in-source
  # fragment and its precursor feature.
  isf_rt2 = 0.01,
  # If TRUE, require the mean fragment/precursor intensity ratio to fall between
  # isf_ratio_min2 and isf_ratio_max2. If FALSE, omit this intensity-ratio
  # condition.
  isf_control_int2 = TRUE,
  # Lower allowed ratio of mean candidate fragment intensity to mean precursor
  # intensity. Used when isf_control_int2 = TRUE.
  isf_ratio_min2 = 0.001,
  # Upper allowed ratio of mean candidate fragment intensity to mean precursor
  # intensity. Used when isf_control_int2 = TRUE.
  isf_ratio_max2 = 2.5,
  # If TRUE, require the candidate fragment m/z in an eligible MS2 spectrum of
  # the precursor; supply spectra to mc_filter_ms(). Support in any eligible
  # spectrum is sufficient. FALSE uses MS1 evidence only.
  isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE,
  # Minimum intensity of a supporting MS2 peak, expressed as a percentage of that
  # spectrum's base peak. For example, 1 means 1 percent. Used when
  # isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE.
  isf_ms2_rel2 = 1,
  # Absolute tolerance in Da between the candidate in-source fragment m/z and a
  # supporting MS2 peak. Used when isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE.
  isf_ms2_mz_tol2 = 0.01,
  # Spectrum metadata field used to match MGF spectra to precursor feature IDs
  # for in-source fragment checking; typically "acquisitionNum".
  isf_mgf_id_field = "acquisitionNum",
  # MISPICKED-ION FILTERING
  # Enable mispicked-ion filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit
  # filters vector overrides this flag; use "mispicked" to select mispicked-ion
  # filtering explicitly.
  enable_mis2 = FALSE,
  # Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of features
  # proposed to be duplicate peak detections. Values range from 0 to 1; higher
  # cutoffs require more similar profiles.
  mis_cor2 = 0.8,
  # Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between features proposed to
  # be duplicate peak detections.
  mis_rt2 = 0.002,
  # Mass-tolerance unit for mispicked-ion matching: "da" uses mis_mz_tol2; "ppm"
  # uses mis_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used.
  mis_tol_type2 = "ppm",
  # Absolute mass tolerance in Da for mispicked-ion matching. Used only when
  # mis_tol_type2 = "da".
  mis_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  # Relative mass tolerance in ppm for mispicked-ion matching. Used only when
  # mis_tol_type2 = "ppm".
  mis_ppm2 = 10,
  # RINGING/SATURATED-ION FILTERING
  # Enable ringing/saturated-ion filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An
  # explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "ringing" to select
  # ringing/saturated-ion filtering explicitly.
  enable_ring2 = FALSE,
  # Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of a
  # candidate ringing artifact and its high-intensity anchor. Values range from 0
  # to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles.
  ring_cor2 = 0.8,
  # Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between a candidate ringing
  # artifact and its high-intensity anchor.
  ring_rt2 = 0.05,
  # Mass-tolerance unit for ringing/saturated-ion matching: "da" uses
  # ring_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses ring_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used.
  ring_tol_type2 = "da",
  # Absolute mass tolerance in Da for ringing/saturated-ion matching. Used only
  # when ring_tol_type2 = "da".
  ring_mz_tol2 = 0.95,
  # Relative mass tolerance in ppm for ringing/saturated-ion matching. Used only
  # when ring_tol_type2 = "ppm".
  ring_ppm2 = 500,
  # Minimum mean sample intensity for a feature to act as the high-intensity
  # anchor in ringing/saturated-ion filtering.
  ring_min_anch2 = 1e+05,
  # Minimum ratio of anchor mean intensity to candidate artifact mean intensity
  # in ringing/saturated-ion filtering. For example, 10 requires the anchor to be
  # at least ten times as intense; must be at least 1.
  ring_ratio2 = 10,
  # If TRUE, search for ringing artifacts below and above the anchor m/z. If
  # FALSE, search only above the anchor m/z.
  ring_bidirectional2 = FALSE
)
```


```{r peak-defaults}
peak_options <- mc_peak_parameters(
  # RMD = 1e6 * (mz - floor(mz + 0.5)) / mz.
  # AMD = abs(mz - floor(mz + 0.5)).
  # Peak filters enabled when mc_filter_peak(filters = NULL): "mz", "rt", "rmd",
  # "amd" and/or "target". An empty vector selects none. An explicit filters
  # vector overrides this setting.
  peak_filters = character(),
  # Enable the lower m/z limit, peak_mz_min, when the "mz" peak filter is
  # selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  mz_min_enable = TRUE,
  # Enable the upper m/z limit, peak_mz_max, when the "mz" peak filter is
  # selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  mz_max_enable = FALSE,
  # Lower m/z limit in m/z units. Keep values greater than or equal to this limit
  # when mz_min_enable = TRUE and the "mz" filter is selected.
  peak_mz_min = 200,
  # Upper m/z limit in m/z units. Keep values less than or equal to this limit
  # when mz_max_enable = TRUE and the "mz" filter is selected.
  peak_mz_max = 1500,
  # Enable the lower retention time limit, peak_rt_min, when the "rt" peak filter
  # is selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  rt_min_enable = TRUE,
  # Enable the upper retention time limit, peak_rt_max, when the "rt" peak filter
  # is selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  rt_max_enable = FALSE,
  # Lower retention time limit in minutes. Keep values greater than or equal to
  # this limit when rt_min_enable = TRUE and the "rt" filter is selected.
  peak_rt_min = 1,
  # Upper retention time limit in minutes. Keep values less than or equal to this
  # limit when rt_max_enable = TRUE and the "rt" filter is selected.
  peak_rt_max = 30,
  # Enable the lower relative mass defect (RMD) limit, peak_rmd_min, when the
  # "rmd" peak filter is selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  rmd_min_enable = TRUE,
  # Enable the upper relative mass defect (RMD) limit, peak_rmd_max, when the
  # "rmd" peak filter is selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  rmd_max_enable = TRUE,
  # Lower relative mass defect (RMD) limit in ppm. Keep values greater than or
  # equal to this limit when rmd_min_enable = TRUE and the "rmd" filter is
  # selected.
  peak_rmd_min = -2000,
  # Upper relative mass defect (RMD) limit in ppm. Keep values less than or equal
  # to this limit when rmd_max_enable = TRUE and the "rmd" filter is selected.
  peak_rmd_max = 2000,
  # Enable the lower absolute mass defect (AMD) limit, peak_amd_min, when the
  # "amd" peak filter is selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  amd_min_enable = TRUE,
  # Enable the upper absolute mass defect (AMD) limit, peak_amd_max, when the
  # "amd" peak filter is selected. FALSE disables this bound only.
  amd_max_enable = TRUE,
  # Lower absolute mass defect (AMD) limit in Da. Keep values greater than or
  # equal to this limit when amd_min_enable = TRUE and the "amd" filter is
  # selected.
  peak_amd_min = 0,
  # Upper absolute mass defect (AMD) limit in Da. Keep values less than or equal
  # to this limit when amd_max_enable = TRUE and the "amd" filter is selected.
  peak_amd_max = 0.5,
  # Action for features matching a target by both m/z and retention time:
  # "remove" discards matches; "keep" retains only matches. Used when the
  # "target" peak filter is selected.
  target_peak_action = "remove",
  # Mass-tolerance unit for target matching: "da" uses target_mz_tol_da; "ppm"
  # uses target_mz_tol_ppm.
  target_mz_tol_type = "da",
  # Absolute m/z tolerance in Da for matching features to targets. Used only when
  # target_mz_tol_type = "da".
  target_mz_tol_da = 0.005,
  # Relative m/z tolerance in ppm for matching features to targets. Used only
  # when target_mz_tol_type = "ppm".
  target_mz_tol_ppm = 10,
  # Maximum retention-time difference in minutes between a feature and a target.
  # Both the m/z and retention-time conditions must pass for a target match.
  target_rt_tol = 0.05
)
```

## QC and blank recipes

QC examples below illustrate options.
`group_any` requires at least one group to pass each metric, `group_every` requires
all selected groups, and `pooled` combines selected samples. Selected metrics are
combined with AND. D-ratio requires a genuine QC group and enough replicate samples.

```{r qc-recipes}
after_blank <- mc_filter_blank(imported, groups = "Blank",
                               mode = "mean_cutoff", cutoff = 0.10)
# Alternative, starting again from imported:
after_detected <- mc_filter_blank(imported, groups = "Blank",
                                  mode = "drop_detected")
after_qc <- mc_filter_qc(
  imported, filters = c("zeros", "mean", "rsd", "min"),
  mode = "group_every", groups = "Sample",
  zero_metric = "percent", zero_cutoff = 50,
  mean_cutoff = 5000, rsd_cutoff = 30, min_cutoff = 1000
)
# For YOUR data with QC replicates:
# after_dratio <- mc_filter_qc(
#   your_data, filters = "dratio", groups = "Sample",
#   mode = "pooled", qc_group = "QC", dratio_cutoff = 50
# )
```

## Labels, column selection and custom targets

```{r alternatives}
# Alternative label sources (choose one):
label_file <- system.file("extdata", "Label.csv",
                          package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE)
imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_csv(label_file, imported$sample_cols)
imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_names(imported$sample_cols,
                                        separator = "_", token = 2)
# Or provide a named vector covering every sample:
my_labels <- setNames(unname(imported$labels), imported$sample_cols)
imported$labels <- my_labels

# Exact names or positions after input-format conversion:
manual <- mc_prepare(peak_file, type = "mzmine",
                      sample_cols = imported$sample_cols)
# sample_cols = c(4, 5, 6) is also allowed: verify your column positions first.

# Illustrative targets:
targets <- data.frame(mz = c(300.123, 450.234), rt = c(5.2, 8.1))
target_options <- mc_peak_parameters(
  target_peak_action = "remove", target_mz_tol_type = "ppm",
  target_mz_tol_ppm = 10, target_rt_tol = 0.05
)
after_target <- mc_filter_peak(imported, filters = "target",
                               parameters = target_options, targets = targets)
after_target$target_matches
# Alternatively: targets = "targets.csv" or
# target_text = "300.123,5.2\n450.234,8.1"

# Optional custom neutral-loss definitions, using YOUR local CSV:
# after_nl <- mc_filter_ms(imported, filters = "neutral_losses",
#   parameters = mc_ms_parameters(nl_pol2 = "negative"),
#   neutral_losses = "neutral_losses.csv")
```

## Functions and arguments

Each template shows the complete argument list. Choice vectors in templates list allowed alternatives; normally select one string. `...` in parameter constructors accepts the named settings listed above.

### mc_prepare

Read a feature-by-sample peak table, identify intensity columns, and assign sample groups. Feature metadata are retained alongside the intensity values.

```{r usage-mc_prepare}
# mc_prepare(data, type = c("mzmine", "generic", "xcms", "msdial"), 
#     sample_cols = NULL, sample_keywords = NULL, id_col = NULL, 
#     mz_col = NULL, rt_col = NULL, labels = NULL, token_sep = "_", 
#     token_index = 2)
```

- `data`: A local CSV filename or a data frame with one feature per row. Bundled files can be located with `system.file()`. For a web-hosted CSV, first read it with `vroom::vroom(url, delim = ",")` and pass the resulting table.
- `type`: Input format: `"mzmine"` (default), `"generic"`, `"xcms"`, or `"msdial"`. XCMS retention times are converted from seconds to minutes. Other formats require retention times in minutes. See [compatible peak-table examples](https://github.com/plyush1993/MetaboCensoR/tree/main/Input_Examples) for the supported input layouts.
- `sample_cols`: Intensity-column names or integer column positions after format conversion and column cleanup. Explicit selections take precedence over `sample_keywords`.
- `sample_keywords`: Case-sensitive literal substrings used to identify intensity columns. A column is selected if its name contains at least one substring. If neither selector is supplied, columns with at least 70% finite numeric entries are considered, excluding identified feature columns and names beginning with row.
- `id_col`: Feature-ID column name. If omitted, searches for row ID, Feature ID, or Alignment ID, then uses the first column. Original names recognized during format conversion may also be supplied.
- `mz_col`: Feature m/z column name. Defaults to the standardized `mz` column; recognized original column names are accepted.
- `rt_col`: Retention-time column name. Defaults to the standardized `rt` column; recognized original column names are accepted.
- `labels`: One nonempty group label per sample. An unnamed vector must follow the selected sample columns; a named vector is matched to their names. If omitted, groups are extracted from sample names using `token_sep` and `token_index`.
- `token_sep`: Literal separator used to split sample names when labels are omitted. Default: `"_"`.
- `token_index`: One-based position of the group name in each split sample name. Default: 2.


### mc_labels_from_names

Split each sample name at a chosen separator and use one part as its group label.

```{r usage-mc_labels_from_names}
# mc_labels_from_names(sample_names, separator = "_", token = 2)
```

- `sample_names`: Character vector of sample-column names, in the required output order.
- `separator`: Literal separator, not a regular expression. Default: `"_"`.
- `token`: Positive integer giving the one-based position of the group name. Default: 2.


### mc_labels_from_metadata

Read sample names and groups from two metadata columns and align the group labels to the peak-table sample order.

```{r usage-mc_labels_from_metadata}
# mc_labels_from_metadata(path, sample_names, sample_col, label_col, clean_names = FALSE, 
#     remove_suffixes = NULL)
```

- `path`: Local metadata CSV filename. The first row must contain column names. Download remote files before calling this function.
- `sample_names`: Sample-column names to match, in the required output order.
- `sample_col`: Exact metadata column name containing sample identifiers.
- `label_col`: Exact metadata column name containing group labels.
- `clean_names`: If `TRUE`, also remove the suffixes specified in `remove_suffixes` from both sets of names before matching. Default: `FALSE`.
- `remove_suffixes`: Optional trailing strings to remove, for example `c(" Peak area", ".mzML")`. Suffix removal is case-insensitive and is used only when `clean_names = TRUE`.


### mc_labels_from_csv

Read a headerless CSV containing one sample-group label per row.

```{r usage-mc_labels_from_csv}
# mc_labels_from_csv(path, sample_names)
```

- `path`: Filename of a comma-separated, headerless label file. The first column is read as the label vector.
- `sample_names`: Sample-column names in the same order as the labels in the file.


### mc_filter_blank

Compare feature intensities in blank and experimental groups, or remove every feature detected in a blank sample. Save the values and decisions for inspection and plotting.

```{r usage-mc_filter_blank}
# mc_filter_blank(x, groups, mode = c("mean_cutoff", "drop_detected"), 
#     cutoff = 0.1, labels = NULL)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `groups`: One or more existing group labels identifying blanks, for example `"Blank"`. All remaining groups are treated as experimental groups in ratio mode.
- `mode`: `"mean_cutoff"` (default) compares blank and experimental group means. `"drop_detected"` removes any feature with intensity greater than zero in any selected blank sample.
- `cutoff`: Nonnegative blank-to-sample ratio threshold, default 0.10. Used only in `"mean_cutoff"` mode. A ratio equal to the cutoff does not pass.
- `labels`: Optional sample-group labels. An unnamed vector must follow `x$sample_cols`; a named vector must cover those sample names exactly. `NULL` uses `x$labels`.


### mc_filter_qc

Calculate zero abundance, mean intensity, relative standard deviation, D-ratio, or minimum intensity for selected sample groups, then retain features that pass every selected metric.

```{r usage-mc_filter_qc}
# mc_filter_qc(x, filters = character(), mode = c("group_any", "group_every", 
#     "pooled"), groups = NULL, zero_metric = c("count", "percent"), 
#     zero_cutoff = 1, mean_cutoff = 5000, rsd_cutoff = 30, min_cutoff = 1000, 
#     qc_group = NULL, dratio_cutoff = 50, labels = NULL)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `filters`: Character vector containing any of `"zeros"`, `"mean"`, `"rsd"`, `"dratio"`, and `"min"`. The default empty vector removes nothing.
- `mode`: `"group_any"` (default): each metric must pass in at least one selected group. `"group_every"`: each metric must pass in every selected group. `"pooled"`: combine selected samples before calculating each metric.
- `groups`: Group labels to evaluate. `NULL` or an empty vector selects all groups. For D-ratio, the group specified by `qc_group` is excluded from the biological denominator. Select biological groups explicitly to avoid including blanks.
- `zero_metric`: Express zeros as `"count"` or `"percent"` of evaluated samples.
- `zero_cutoff`: 	Zero-count or zero-percentage threshold. Default: 1. Features pass only when their zero count or percentage is strictly less than this threshold. With `"zero_metric"` = `"count"`, a cutoff of 1 allows no zeros. With `"zero_metric"` = `"percent"`, a cutoff of 50 rejects features with exactly 50 percent zeros.
- `mean_cutoff`: Minimum arithmetic mean intensity. Equality passes. Default: 5000.
- `rsd_cutoff`: Maximum RSD in percent. Equality passes. Default: 30.
- `min_cutoff`: Minimum observed intensity. Equality passes. Default: 1000.
- `qc_group`: Exactly one existing pooled-QC group label for D-ratio, containing at least two samples. Required only when dratio is selected.
- `dratio_cutoff`: Maximum D-ratio in percent. Equality passes. Default: 50.
- `labels`: Optional sample-group labels. An unnamed vector must follow `x$sample_cols`; a named vector must cover those sample names exactly. `NULL` uses `x$labels`.


### mc_filter_ms

Apply isotope, adduct, neutral-loss, in-source-fragment, mispicked-ion, and ringing-artifact filters. Retain representative features and expose the annotation tables for inspection.

```{r usage-mc_filter_ms}
# mc_filter_ms(x, filters = NULL, parameters = mc_ms_parameters(), 
#     adducts = NULL, neutral_losses = NULL, spectra = NULL)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `filters`: Any of `"isotopes"`, `"adducts"`, `"neutral_losses"`, `"isf"`, `"mispicked"`, and `"ringing"`. An explicit vector overrides enable flags in parameters. `NULL` uses those flags; isotopes and adducts are enabled by default. `character(0)` disables all subfilters.
- `parameters`: Named list from `mc_ms_parameters()`. Pass your list explicitly with `parameters = ms_options`.
- `adducts`: Custom adduct data frame or local CSV filename. NULL uses built-in definitions. Required columns are described below.
- `neutral_losses`: Custom neutral-loss data frame or local CSV filename. NULL uses built-in definitions. Required columns are described below.
- `spectra`: A `Spectra` object, for example from `mc_read_mgf()`. Required for ISF when MS2 checking is enabled.


### mc_filter_peak

Apply selected feature-property bounds or match a list of m/z and retention-time targets. Store values and filtering decisions for plotting.

```{r usage-mc_filter_peak}
# mc_filter_peak(x, filters = NULL, parameters = mc_peak_parameters(), 
#     targets = NULL, target_text = NULL)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `filters`: Any of `"mz"`, `"rt"`, `"rmd"`, `"amd"`, and `"target"`. `NULL` uses `parameters$peak_filters`; the default selects no filters.
- `parameters`: Named list from `mc_peak_parameters()`, specifying enabled bounds and target-matching tolerances.
- `targets`: Target data frame or local CSV filename with m/z and retention time in minutes. Use columns named `mz` and `rt`; if recognizable names are absent, the first two columns are used.
- `target_text`: Optional comma-separated target rows as one string, with or without a header. These rows are combined with targets and duplicate m/z-RT pairs are removed.


### mc_ms_parameters

Create a complete named list of MS-filter settings, replacing selected defaults with your named arguments.

```{r usage-mc_ms_parameters}
# mc_ms_parameters(...)
```

- `...`: Named settings to replace. Supported names, meanings, units, and defaults are listed below. Unknown names raise an error.


### mc_peak_parameters

Create a complete named list of peak-filter settings with selected defaults replaced.

```{r usage-mc_peak_parameters}
# mc_peak_parameters(...)
```

- `...`: Named settings to replace. Supported names, meanings, units, and defaults are listed below. Unknown names raise an error.


### mc_read_mgf

Import an MGF file as a Spectra object for fragment confirmation or synchronized peak-table and spectral export.

```{r usage-mc_read_mgf}
# mc_read_mgf(path)
```

- `path`: Local MGF filename. Download a remote MGF to a local file before reading it.


### mc_filter_mgf

Subset a Spectra object using the feature IDs in a filtered result or a supplied table.

```{r usage-mc_filter_mgf}
# mc_filter_mgf(spectra, table, match_col = NULL, id_field = "acquisitionNum")
```

- `spectra`: A `Spectra` object to subset.
- `table`: A `metabocensor_result` or a data frame identifying the features to retain.
- `match_col`: Feature-ID column. With a result object, `NULL` uses its selected ID column; with a data frame, `NULL` uses the first column. An explicit name for a result object refers to the input-format exported table.
- `id_field`: Spectrum metadata field containing feature IDs. Default: `"acquisitionNum"`.


### mc_write_mgf

Export a Spectra object to a specified MGF file.

```{r usage-mc_write_mgf}
# mc_write_mgf(spectra, path)
```

- `spectra`: A `Spectra` object to export.
- `path`: Output MGF filename, including the desired directory. An existing file may be overwritten.


### mc_final_table

Return retained features as a data frame in the original, standardized, or internal layout.

```{r usage-mc_final_table}
# mc_final_table(x, format = c("input", "standard", "internal"))
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `format`: Output layout: `"input"` restores original column names and order, metadata columns, and XCMS retention times in seconds; `"standard"` returns Feature ID, mz, rt in minutes, and sample intensities; `"internal"` returns the current table including `.FID`.


### mc_write_table

Export retained features to a CSV file with a chosen column layout.

```{r usage-mc_write_table}
# mc_write_table(x, path, format = c("input", "standard", "internal"))
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `path`: Output CSV filename, including the desired directory. Existing output is overwritten.
- `format`: Output layout: `"input"` restores original column names and order, metadata columns, and XCMS retention times in seconds; `"standard"` returns Feature ID, mz, rt in minutes, and sample intensities; `"internal"` returns the current table including `.FID`.


### mc_export

Collect the current filtered peak table and optionally retain matching MGF spectra. Write either or both outputs when filenames are supplied.

```{r usage-mc_export}
# mc_export(x, csv = NULL, mgf = NULL, mgf_file = NULL, id_field = "acquisitionNum", 
#     match_col = NULL, format = c("input", "standard", "internal"))
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `csv`: Optional output CSV filename. NULL returns the table without writing a CSV.
- `mgf`: Optional local MGF filename or `Spectra` object. Spectra are matched to retained feature IDs.
- `mgf_file`: Optional output MGF filename. Requires `mgf`.
- `id_field`: Spectrum metadata field containing feature IDs. Default: `"acquisitionNum"`.
- `match_col`: Optional ID column in the exported table. `NULL` uses the ID column selected at import, regardless of output layout.
- `format`: Output layout: `"input"` restores original column names and order, metadata columns, and XCMS retention times in seconds; `"standard"` returns Feature ID, mz, rt in minutes, and sample intensities; `"internal"` returns the current table including `.FID`.


### mc_run

Apply selected filtering stages in the fixed order blank, MS, QC, and peak filtering.

```{r usage-mc_run}
# mc_run(x, blank = NULL, ms = NULL, qc = NULL, peak = NULL)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `blank`: `NULL` to skip blank filtering, or a named list of arguments to `mc_filter_blank()` other than x.
- `ms`: `NULL` to skip MS filtering, or a named list of arguments to `mc_filter_ms()` other than x.
- `qc`: `NULL` to skip QC filtering, or a named list of arguments to `mc_filter_qc()` other than x.
- `peak`: `NULL` to skip peak filtering, or a named list of arguments to `mc_filter_peak()` other than x.


### mc_summary

Return feature counts before and after each completed filtering stage.

```{r usage-mc_summary}
# mc_summary(x)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.


### print.metabocensor_result

Display the current numbers of features and samples, followed by stage-level filtering counts.

```{r usage-print-metabocensor_result}
# print(x, ...)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `...`: Additional arguments; currently unused.


### mc_plot_blank

Visualize the saved blank comparisons and filtering threshold.

```{r usage-mc_plot_blank}
# mc_plot_blank(x, interactive = TRUE)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `interactive`: `TRUE` returns an interactive Plotly figure. `FALSE` returns static ggplot output.


### mc_plot_qc

Visualize the saved QC values and their filtering thresholds.

```{r usage-mc_plot_qc}
# mc_plot_qc(x, filters = NULL, interactive = TRUE)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `filters`: QC metrics to display: zeros, mean, rsd, dratio, or min. Only metrics already stored by `mc_filter_qc()` can be selected. NULL displays all stored metrics.
- `interactive`: `TRUE` returns an interactive Plotly figure. `FALSE` returns static ggplot output.


### mc_plot_peak

Visualize the saved m/z, retention times, and mass defects.

```{r usage-mc_plot_peak}
# mc_plot_peak(x, filters = NULL, interactive = TRUE, webgl = TRUE)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `filters`: Properties to display: mz, rt, rmd, or amd. NULL selects the corresponding filters used in the peak-filtering step. Target matching has no scatter plot.
- `interactive`: `TRUE` returns an interactive Plotly figure. `FALSE` returns static ggplot output.
- `webgl`: Use WebGL for interactive scatter traces. Ignored for static output.


### mc_plot_ms

Visualize the saved number of features removed by each MS subfilter.

```{r usage-mc_plot_ms}
# mc_plot_ms(x, interactive = TRUE)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `interactive`: `TRUE` returns an interactive Plotly figure. `FALSE` returns static ggplot output.


### mc_plot_summary

Visualize the saved number of retained features after each filtering stage.

```{r usage-mc_plot_summary}
# mc_plot_summary(x, interactive = TRUE)
```

- `x`: A `metabocensor_result` returned by `mc_prepare()` or a filtering function.
- `interactive`: `TRUE` returns an interactive Plotly figure. `FALSE` returns static ggplot output.

## Results, annotation tables and plots

Each stage can be applied once to an object. To change a stage, start from the saved
object before that stage. Individual calls can use different stage orders;
`mc_run()` always uses blank, MS, QC, then peak. MS subfilters have their own fixed order.

```{r results}
after_ms <- mc_filter_ms(
  after_blank, filters = c("isotopes", "adducts", "isf"),
  parameters = ms_options, spectra = spectra, adducts = adduct_file
)
mc_summary(after_ms)
print(after_ms)
after_ms$ms$counts
after_ms$removed_ids
after_ms$annot_tbls$iso_table
after_ms$annot_tbls$add_table
after_ms$annot_tbls$nl_table
after_ms$annot_tbls$isf_table
after_ms$annot_tbls$mis_table
after_ms$annot_tbls$ring_table
# A table can be NULL when its filter was not run.
after_blank$blank_tbl
after_qc$qc_tbl

# Plot stored results without recalculating filters.
mc_plot_blank(after_blank, interactive = FALSE)
mc_plot_ms(after_ms, interactive = TRUE)
mc_plot_qc(after_qc, filters = "rsd", interactive = FALSE)
mc_plot_summary(after_ms, interactive = FALSE)
```
